rule: flaky waits: wait on state, never sleep
problem: After typing in the search box the test sleeps 1000 ms before asserting the rows.
impact: Too short on a slow runner, wasted time on a fast one; the web-first assertions below already wait for the rows.

rule: flaky waits: wait on state, never networkidle
problem: The sort test waits for `networkidle` before asserting the first row.
impact: `networkidle` is a time heuristic (and the page may keep connections open); the assertion that follows should wait on the row itself.

rule: locators: getByRole/getByLabel first, never CSS classes
problem: The first row is found with the Ant Design class `.ant-table-row` plus `.first()`, although rows have the `row` role.
impact: A library upgrade or restyle changes the class and breaks the spec; `.first()` over a shared list also pins whatever order the data has.

rule: e2e auth through a setup project and storageState; specs never depend on each other
problem: The sign-in test is an ordinary spec that writes `e2e/.auth/user.json`, and `customers.spec.ts` reads it with `test.use({ storageState })`; the config has no setup project or dependency.
impact: With `fullyParallel` the customers specs can start before the file exists, or run alone with no session; running one spec in isolation fails.

rule: flaky waits fixed by waiting on state, never retry or longer timeout
problem: The config sets `retries: 3`, a 90 s test timeout and a 20 s expect timeout to ride out a slow dev API.
impact: Flaky tests pass on a retry and are never fixed, genuine failures take minutes to show, and every assertion hides real latency regressions.

problem: `test.only` is left on the minimum-order test.
impact: Every other test in the file is silently skipped, so the suite stays green with most of the coverage gone (and `forbidOnly` is not set).
quote: test.only("hides customers under the minimum order count"

rule: screenshot tests only with an existing visual setup and a stable surface
problem: `toHaveScreenshot` on the full customers page, which shows live rows and totals, with no mask and no committed visual baseline or visual project.
impact: The first run only writes a baseline and later runs fail on data or font changes, producing noise rather than regressions.

rule: specs never depend on each other
problem: The "search box" tests run in serial mode on one shared page; "clearing the search" clicks the clear button that only exists because the previous test typed "ada".
impact: The second test fails when run alone, is skipped after the first fails, and cannot be sharded.
quote: test("clearing the search brings every customer back"
